lede: Oil up 5% on Hurricane Isaias, Hormuz attacks and Iran strike-option reports; Fed minutes lean to another hike.

single_name_moves.venue: Wed close, nearly -6%, weighed on the Dow (Investopedia)

geo_headlines: OIL UP 5%: BRENT BACK ABOVE $105. Brent December is $105.22 (+5.0%) and WTI November $92.65 (+5.0%) as of 7:05 AM ET. Three drivers: Hurricane Isaias is heading for the Gulf Coast, with about 25% of Gulf crude output shut in (Plastics News, citing producers); attacks on tankers pushed Hormuz traffic to its lowest in more than two months (Iran International, citing Reuters); and reports say the White House asked the Pentagon for Iran strike options before the November 3 midterms (The Atlantic, Axios). **Brent is now at the $105 line the client frame flags.**

FED MINUTES: MOST SEE ANOTHER HIKE BY YEAR END. The September minutes said "most participants" judged another increase "would likely be appropriate by year end," with inflation risks seen to the upside (Investopedia, TD Economics). FedWatch: October hike odds 17.7%, from 21.0%; December 84.3%.

STRONG 10-YEAR AUCTION CAPPED YIELDS. The $39 billion 10-year sold at 5.300% with a 2.77 bid-to-cover, well above the 2.52 average (RTTNews). The 10-year touched about 5.37% before the sale, then closed at 5.28% (+1bp) on Treasury's curve; the 30-year closed at 5.67%, above Monday's 5.66%. The $22 billion 30-year auction is today.

STOCKS SLIPPED FROM RECORDS. The S&P 500 fell 0.22% to 7,801.77, the Nasdaq 100 0.21% and the Composite 0.22%; the Dow fell 0.66% as Caterpillar dropped nearly 6% (Investopedia). Chip stocks fell about 1.1%.

FUTURES LOWER; ASIA DOWN; BITCOIN WEAKER. S&P 500 futures 7,809 (-0.56%), Nasdaq 100 futures 31,145.75 (-0.82%) as of 6:55 AM ET. Asian shares fell on rising yields and oil (AP). Bitcoin $82,554 (-0.9%). Gold $4,143.90 (+0.1%).

TODAY: CLAIMS, PEPSICO, 30-YEAR AUCTION. Jobless claims 8:30 AM (consensus 200k), wholesale inventories 10:00, St. Louis Fed President Musalem 1:40 PM, the 30-year auction, and PepsiCo before the open (ZeroHedge, MarketBeat).
client_frame_short: Oil is the story this morning. Brent jumped 5% to about $105 as a hurricane heads for Gulf oil platforms, tanker attacks slowed traffic through Hormuz, and reports say the White House asked for Iran strike options. **Yesterday's Fed minutes said most officials expect another rate hike by year end, so higher oil makes that more likely, not less.** Stocks slipped from records and futures are lower. For clients, nothing here calls for changes, but this is the day to watch the $105 oil line and the 30-year auction.
client_frame:
If a client calls this morning, the story is oil, and why it matters for rates.

Oil: Brent rose about 5% overnight to roughly $105. Three things hit at once. Hurricane Isaias is heading for the Gulf Coast, and producers have shut in about a quarter of Gulf crude output. Tanker attacks cut traffic through the Strait of Hormuz to the lowest in more than two months. And news reports say the White House asked the Pentagon for Iran strike options before the midterms. No decision has been reported. A storm is a short-lived supply hit; a return to strikes on Iran would be a longer one.

The Fed: Wednesday's minutes said most officials see another hike as likely appropriate by year end. Markets still put October odds below one in five, with December near 84%. Higher oil feeds inflation, which supports that path.

Bonds: the 10-year touched about 5.37% before a strong auction pulled it back to 5.28% at the close. Demand was well above average. That is a useful sign that buyers show up at these yields. The 30-year closed at 5.67%, a hair above Monday's level, ahead of today's 30-year auction.

Stocks: the S&P 500 slipped 0.2% from Tuesday's record, and futures are lower this morning. Earnings season starts next week with the banks, and analysts expect third-quarter profits up about 30%. Records built on earnings are sturdier than records built on hope.

Why it matters: oil near $105 and long yields near 5.7% are the two forces most likely to test stock valuations. Neither has broken its line yet.

For clients, the message holds: high-quality bonds pay more than 5% for a decade, and long-term equity plans do not need changing. What would change the view: a 10-year close above 5.40% (now 5.28%), a 30-year above 5.75% (now 5.67%), or actual US strikes on Iran that keep Brent well above $105. Brent is at that line this morning, so we're watching it, but strike options are planning, not action.
